<dd>Compile for <font SIZE="-1">ARC 600 CPU</font> with <tt>&quot;norm&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;mul64&quot;</tt>-family instructions enabled.
<dt><b>arc601_norm</b>
<dd>Compile for <font SIZE="-1">ARC 601 CPU</font> with <tt>&quot;norm&quot;</tt> instructions enabled.
<dt><b>arc601_mul32x16</b>
<dd>Compile for <font SIZE="-1">ARC 601 CPU</font> with <tt>&quot;norm&quot;</tt> and 32x16-bit multiply instructions enabled.
<dt><b>arc601_mul64</b>
<dd>Compile for <font SIZE="-1">ARC 601 CPU</font> with <tt>&quot;norm&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;mul64&quot;</tt>-family instructions enabled.
<dt><b>nps400</b>
<dd>Compile for <font SIZE="-1">ARC 700</font> on <font SIZE="-1">NPS400</font> chip.
<dt><b>em_mini</b>
<dd>Compile for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM</font> minimalist configuration featuring reduced register set.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-mdpfp</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mdpfp-compact</b>
<dd>Generate double-precision <font SIZE="-1">FPX</font> instructions, tuned for the compact implementation.
<dt><b>-mdpfp-fast</b>
<dd>Generate double-precision <font SIZE="-1">FPX</font> instructions, tuned for the fast implementation.
<dt><b>-mno-dpfp-lrsr</b>
<dd>Disable <tt>&quot;lr&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;sr&quot;</tt> instructions from using <font SIZE="-1">FPX</font> extension aux registers.
<dt><b>-mea</b>
<dd>Generate extended arithmetic instructions. Currently only <tt>&quot;divaw&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;adds&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;subs&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;sat16&quot;</tt> are supported. This is always enabled for <b>-mcpu=ARC700</b>.
<dt><b>-mno-mpy</b>
<dd>Do not generate <tt>&quot;mpy&quot;</tt>-family instructions for <font SIZE="-1">ARC700.</font> This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mmul32x16</b>
<dd>Generate 32x16-bit multiply and multiply-accumulate instructions.
<dt><b>-mmul64</b>
<dd>Generate <tt>&quot;mul64&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;mulu64&quot;</tt> instructions. Only valid for <b>-mcpu=ARC600</b>.
<dt><b>-mnorm</b>
<dd>Generate <tt>&quot;norm&quot;</tt> instructions. This is the default if <b>-mcpu=ARC700</b> is in effect.
<dt><b>-mspfp</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mspfp-compact</b>
<dd>Generate single-precision <font SIZE="-1">FPX</font> instructions, tuned for the compact implementation.
<dt><b>-mspfp-fast</b>
<dd>Generate single-precision <font SIZE="-1">FPX</font> instructions, tuned for the fast implementation.
<dt><b>-msimd</b>
<dd>Enable generation of <font SIZE="-1">ARC SIMD</font> instructions via target-specific builtins. Only valid for <b>-mcpu=ARC700</b>.
<dt><b>-msoft-float</b>
<dd>This option ignored; it is provided for compatibility purposes only. Software floating-point code is emitted by default, and this default can overridden by <font SIZE="-1">FPX</font> options; <b>-mspfp</b>, <b>-mspfp-compact</b>, or <b>-mspfp-fast</b> for single precision, and <b>-mdpfp</b>, <b>-mdpfp-compact</b>, or <b>-mdpfp-fast</b> for double precision.
<dt><b>-mswap</b>
<dd>Generate <tt>&quot;swap&quot;</tt> instructions.
<dt><b>-matomic</b>
<dd>This enables use of the locked load/store conditional extension to implement atomic memory built-in functions. Not available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC</font> 6xx or <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM</font> cores.
<dt><b>-mdiv-rem</b>
<dd>Enable <tt>&quot;div&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;rem&quot;</tt> instructions for ARCv2 cores.
<dt><b>-mcode-density</b>
<dd>Enable code density instructions for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font> This option is on by default for <font SIZE="-1">ARC HS.</font>
<dt><b>-mll64</b>
<dd>Enable double load/store operations for <font SIZE="-1">ARC HS</font> cores.
<dt><b>-mtp-regno=</b><i>regno</i>
<dd>Specify thread pointer register number.
<dt><b>-mmpy-option=</b><i>multo</i>
<dd>Compile ARCv2 code with a multiplier design option. You can specify the option using either a string or numeric value for <i>multo</i>. <b>wlh1</b> is the default value. The recognized values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>No multiplier available.
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>w</b>
<dd>16x16 multiplier, fully pipelined. The following instructions are enabled: <tt>&quot;mpyw&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;mpyuw&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd><dt><b>wlh1</b>
<dd>32x32 multiplier, fully pipelined (1 stage). The following instructions are additionally enabled: <tt>&quot;mpy&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpyu&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpym&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpymu&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;mpy_s&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>3</b>
<dd><dt><b>wlh2</b>
<dd>32x32 multiplier, fully pipelined (2 stages). The following instructions are additionally enabled: <tt>&quot;mpy&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpyu&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpym&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpymu&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;mpy_s&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>4</b>
<dd><dt><b>wlh3</b>
<dd>Two 16x16 multipliers, blocking, sequential. The following instructions are additionally enabled: <tt>&quot;mpy&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpyu&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpym&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpymu&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;mpy_s&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>5</b>
<dd><dt><b>wlh4</b>
<dd>One 16x16 multiplier, blocking, sequential. The following instructions are additionally enabled: <tt>&quot;mpy&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpyu&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpym&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpymu&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;mpy_s&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>6</b>
<dd><dt><b>wlh5</b>
<dd>One 32x4 multiplier, blocking, sequential. The following instructions are additionally enabled: <tt>&quot;mpy&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpyu&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpym&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;mpymu&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;mpy_s&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>7</b>
<dd><dt><b>plus_dmpy</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">ARC HS SIMD</font> support.
<dt><b>8</b>
<dd><dt><b>plus_macd</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">ARC HS SIMD</font> support.
<dt><b>9</b>
<dd><dt><b>plus_qmacw</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">ARC HS SIMD</font> support.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>This option is only available for ARCv2 cores.</dl><dt><b>-mfpu=</b><i>fpu</i>
<dd>Enables support for specific floating-point hardware extensions for ARCv2 cores. Supported values for <i>fpu</i> are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>fpus</b>
<dd>Enables support for single-precision floating-point hardware extensions.
<dt><b>fpud</b>
<dd>Enables support for double-precision floating-point hardware extensions. The single-precision floating-point extension is also enabled. Not available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font>
<dt><b>fpuda</b>
<dd>Enables support for double-precision floating-point hardware extensions using double-precision assist instructions. The single-precision floating-point extension is also enabled. This option is only available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font>
<dt><b>fpuda_div</b>
<dd>Enables support for double-precision floating-point hardware extensions using double-precision assist instructions. The single-precision floating-point, square-root, and divide extensions are also enabled. This option is only available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font>
<dt><b>fpuda_fma</b>
<dd>Enables support for double-precision floating-point hardware extensions using double-precision assist instructions. The single-precision floating-point and fused multiply and add hardware extensions are also enabled. This option is only available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font>
<dt><b>fpuda_all</b>
<dd>Enables support for double-precision floating-point hardware extensions using double-precision assist instructions. All single-precision floating-point hardware extensions are also enabled. This option is only available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font>
<dt><b>fpus_div</b>
<dd>Enables support for single-precision floating-point, square-root and divide hardware extensions.
<dt><b>fpud_div</b>
<dd>Enables support for double-precision floating-point, square-root and divide hardware extensions. This option includes option <b>fpus_div</b>. Not available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font>
<dt><b>fpus_fma</b>
<dd>Enables support for single-precision floating-point and fused multiply and add hardware extensions.
<dt><b>fpud_fma</b>
<dd>Enables support for double-precision floating-point and fused multiply and add hardware extensions. This option includes option <b>fpus_fma</b>. Not available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font>
<dt><b>fpus_all</b>
<dd>Enables support for all single-precision floating-point hardware extensions.
<dt><b>fpud_all</b>
<dd>Enables support for all single- and double-precision floating-point hardware extensions. Not available for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM.</font></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-mirq-ctrl-saved=</b><i>register-range</i><b>,</b> <i>blink</i><b>,</b> <i>lp_count</i>
<dd>Specifies general-purposes registers that the processor automatically saves/restores on interrupt entry and exit. <i>register-range</i> is specified as two registers separated by a dash. The register range always starts with <tt>&quot;r0&quot;</tt>, the upper limit is <tt>&quot;fp&quot;</tt> register. <i>blink</i> and <i>lp_count</i> are optional. This option is only valid for <font SIZE="-1">ARC EM</font> and <font SIZE="-1">ARC HS</font> cores.
<dt><b>-mrgf-banked-regs=</b><i>number</i>
<dd>Specifies the number of registers replicated in second register bank on entry to fast interrupt. Fast interrupts are interrupts with the highest priority level P0. These interrupts save only <font SIZE="-1">PC</font> and <font SIZE="-1">STATUS32</font> registers to avoid memory transactions during interrupt entry and exit sequences. Use this option when you are using fast interrupts in an <font SIZE="-1">ARC V2</font> family processor. Permitted values are 4, 8, 16, and 32.
<dt><b>-mlpc-width=</b><i>width</i>
<dd>Specify the width of the <tt>&quot;lp_count&quot;</tt> register. Valid values for <i>width</i> are 8, 16, 20, 24, 28 and 32 bits. The default width is fixed to 32 bits. If the width is less than 32, the compiler does not attempt to transform loops in your program to use the zero-delay loop mechanism unless it is known that the <tt>&quot;lp_count&quot;</tt> register can hold the required loop-counter value. Depending on the width specified, the compiler and run-time library might continue to use the loop mechanism for various needs. This option defines macro <tt>&quot;__ARC_LPC_WIDTH__&quot;</tt> with the value of <i>width</i>.
<dt><b>-mrf16</b>
<dd>This option instructs the compiler to generate code for a 16-entry register file. This option defines the <tt>&quot;__ARC_RF16__&quot;</tt> preprocessor macro.
<dt><b>-mbranch-index</b>
<dd>Enable use of <tt>&quot;bi&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;bih&quot;</tt> instructions to implement jump tables.</dl>
 

 The following options are passed through to the assembler, and also define preprocessor macro symbols.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-mdsp-packa</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler to enable the <font SIZE="-1">DSP</font> Pack A extensions. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xdsp_packa&quot;</tt>. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mdvbf</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler to enable the dual Viterbi butterfly extension. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xdvbf&quot;</tt>. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mlock</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler to enable the locked load/store conditional extension. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xlock&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>-mmac-d16</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xxmac_d16&quot;</tt>. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mmac-24</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xxmac_24&quot;</tt>. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mrtsc</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler to enable the 64-bit time-stamp counter extension instruction. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xrtsc&quot;</tt>. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mswape</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler to enable the swap byte ordering extension instruction. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xswape&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>-mtelephony</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler to enable dual- and single-operand instructions for telephony. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xtelephony&quot;</tt>. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mxy</b>
<dd>Passed down to the assembler to enable the <font SIZE="-1">XY</font> memory extension. Also sets the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__Xxy&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 The following options control how the assembly code is annotated:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-misize</b>
<dd>Annotate assembler instructions with estimated addresses.
<dt><b>-mannotate-align</b>
<dd>Explain what alignment considerations lead to the decision to make an instruction short or long.</dl>
 

 The following options are passed through to the linker:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-marclinux</b>
<dd>Passed through to the linker, to specify use of the <tt>&quot;arclinux&quot;</tt> emulation. This option is enabled by default in tool chains built for <tt>&quot;arc-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;arceb-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> targets when profiling is not requested.
<dt><b>-marclinux_prof</b>
<dd>Passed through to the linker, to specify use of the <tt>&quot;arclinux_prof&quot;</tt> emulation. This option is enabled by default in tool chains built for <tt>&quot;arc-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;arceb-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> targets when profiling is requested.</dl>
 

 The following options control the semantics of generated code:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-mlong-calls</b>
<dd>Generate calls as register indirect calls, thus providing access to the full 32-bit address range.
<dt><b>-mmedium-calls</b>
<dd>Don't use less than 25-bit addressing range for calls, which is the offset available for an unconditional branch-and-link instruction. Conditional execution of function calls is suppressed, to allow use of the 25-bit range, rather than the 21-bit range with conditional branch-and-link. This is the default for tool chains built for <tt>&quot;arc-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;arceb-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> targets.
<dt><b>-G</b> <i>num</i>
<dd>Put definitions of externally-visible data in a small data section if that data is no bigger than <i>num</i> bytes. The default value of <i>num</i> is 4 for any <font SIZE="-1">ARC</font> configuration, or 8 when we have double load/store operations.
<dt><b>-mno-sdata</b>
<dd>Do not generate sdata references. This is the default for tool chains built for <tt>&quot;arc-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;arceb-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> targets.
<dt><b>-mvolatile-cache</b>
<dd>Use ordinarily cached memory accesses for volatile references. This is the default.
<dt><b>-mno-volatile-cache</b>
<dd>Enable cache bypass for volatile references.</dl>
 

 The following options fine tune code generation:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-malign-call</b>
<dd>Do alignment optimizations for call instructions.
<dt><b>-mauto-modify-reg</b>
<dd>Enable the use of pre/post modify with register displacement.
<dt><b>-mbbit-peephole</b>
<dd>Enable bbit peephole2.
<dt><b>-mno-brcc</b>
<dd>This option disables a target-specific pass in <i>arc_reorg</i> to generate compare-and-branch (<tt>&quot;br</tt>cc<tt>&quot;</tt>) instructions. It has no effect on generation of these instructions driven by the combiner pass.
<dt><b>-mcase-vector-pcrel</b>
<dd>Use PC-relative switch case tables to enable case table shortening. This is the default for <b>-Os</b>.
<dt><b>-mcompact-casesi</b>
<dd>Enable compact <tt>&quot;casesi&quot;</tt> pattern. This is the default for <b>-Os</b>, and only available for ARCv1 cores. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mno-cond-exec</b>
<dd>Disable the ARCompact-specific pass to generate conditional execution instructions. 

 Due to delay slot scheduling and interactions between operand numbers, literal sizes, instruction lengths, and the support for conditional execution, the target-independent pass to generate conditional execution is often lacking, so the <font SIZE="-1">ARC</font> port has kept a special pass around that tries to find more conditional execution generation opportunities after register allocation, branch shortening, and delay slot scheduling have been done. This pass generally, but not always, improves performance and code size, at the cost of extra compilation time, which is why there is an option to switch it off. If you have a problem with call instructions exceeding their allowable offset range because they are conditionalized, you should consider using <b>-mmedium-calls</b> instead.
<dt><b>-mearly-cbranchsi</b>
<dd>Enable pre-reload use of the <tt>&quot;cbranchsi&quot;</tt> pattern.
<dt><b>-mexpand-adddi</b>
<dd>Expand <tt>&quot;adddi3&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;subdi3&quot;</tt> at <font SIZE="-1">RTL</font> generation time into <tt>&quot;add.f&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;adc&quot;</tt> etc. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mindexed-loads</b>
<dd>Enable the use of indexed loads. This can be problematic because some optimizers then assume that indexed stores exist, which is not the case.
<dt><b>-mlra</b>
<dd>Enable Local Register Allocation. This is still experimental for <font SIZE="-1">ARC,</font> so by default the compiler uses standard reload (i.e. <b>-mno-lra</b>).
<dt><b>-mlra-priority-none</b>
<dd>Don't indicate any priority for target registers.
<dt><b>-mlra-priority-compact</b>
<dd>Indicate target register priority for r0..r3 / r12..r15.
<dt><b>-mlra-priority-noncompact</b>
<dd>Reduce target register priority for r0..r3 / r12..r15.
<dt><b>-mmillicode</b>
<dd>When optimizing for size (using <b>-Os</b>), prologues and epilogues that have to save or restore a large number of registers are often shortened by using call to a special function in libgcc; this is referred to as a <i>millicode</i> call. As these calls can pose performance issues, and/or cause linking issues when linking in a nonstandard way, this option is provided to turn on or off millicode call generation.
<dt><b>-mcode-density-frame</b>
<dd>This option enable the compiler to emit <tt>&quot;enter&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;leave&quot;</tt> instructions. These instructions are only valid for CPUs with code-density feature.
<dt><b>-mmixed-code</b>
<dd>Tweak register allocation to help 16-bit instruction generation. This generally has the effect of decreasing the average instruction size while increasing the instruction count.
<dt><b>-mq-class</b>
<dd>Enable <b>q</b> instruction alternatives. This is the default for <b>-Os</b>.
<dt><b>-mRcq</b>
<dd>Enable <b>Rcq</b> constraint handling. Most short code generation depends on this. This is the default.
<dt><b>-mRcw</b>
<dd>Enable <b>Rcw</b> constraint handling. Most ccfsm condexec mostly depends on this. This is the default.
<dt><b>-msize-level=</b><i>level</i>
<dd>Fine-tune size optimization with regards to instruction lengths and alignment. The recognized values for <i>level</i> are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd>No size optimization. This level is deprecated and treated like <b>1</b>.
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd>Short instructions are used opportunistically.
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd>In addition, alignment of loops and of code after barriers are dropped.
<dt><b>3</b>
<dd>In addition, optional data alignment is dropped, and the option <b>Os</b> is enabled.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>This defaults to <b>3</b> when <b>-Os</b> is in effect. Otherwise, the behavior when this is not set is equivalent to level <b>1</b>.</dl><dt><b>-mtune=</b><i>cpu</i>
<dd>Set instruction scheduling parameters for <i>cpu</i>, overriding any implied by <b>-mcpu=</b>. 

 Supported values for <i>cpu</i> are
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC600</b></font>
<dd>Tune for <font SIZE="-1">ARC600 CPU.</font>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC601</b></font>
<dd>Tune for <font SIZE="-1">ARC601 CPU.</font>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC700</b></font>
<dd>Tune for <font SIZE="-1">ARC700 CPU</font> with standard multiplier block.
<dt><b>ARC700-xmac</b>
<dd>Tune for <font SIZE="-1">ARC700 CPU</font> with <font SIZE="-1">XMAC</font> block.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC725D</b></font>
<dd>Tune for <font SIZE="-1">ARC725D CPU.</font>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC750D</b></font>
<dd>Tune for <font SIZE="-1">ARC750D CPU.</font></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-mmultcost=</b><i>num</i>
<dd>Cost to assume for a multiply instruction, with <b>4</b> being equal to a normal instruction.
<dt><b>-munalign-prob-threshold=</b><i>probability</i>
<dd>Set probability threshold for unaligning branches. When tuning for <font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC700</b></font> and optimizing for speed, branches without filled delay slot are preferably emitted unaligned and long, unless profiling indicates that the probability for the branch to be taken is below <i>probability</i>. The default is (<font SIZE="-1">REG_BR_PROB_BASE/2</font>), i.e. 5000.</dl>
 

 The following options are maintained for backward compatibility, but are now deprecated and will be removed in a future release:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-margonaut</b>
<dd>Obsolete <font SIZE="-1">FPX.</font>
<dt><b>-mbig-endian</b>
<dd><dt><b>-EB</b>
<dd>Compile code for big-endian targets. Use of these options is now deprecated. Big-endian code is supported by configuring <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> to build <tt>&quot;arceb-elf32&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;arceb-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> targets, for which big endian is the default.
<dt><b>-mlittle-endian</b>
<dd><dt><b>-EL</b>
<dd>Compile code for little-endian targets. Use of these options is now deprecated. Little-endian code is supported by configuring <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> to build <tt>&quot;arc-elf32&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;arc-linux-uclibc&quot;</tt> targets, for which little endian is the default.
<dt><b>-mbarrel_shifter</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mbarrel-shifter</b>.
<dt><b>-mdpfp_compact</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mdpfp-compact</b>.
<dt><b>-mdpfp_fast</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mdpfp-fast</b>.
<dt><b>-mdsp_packa</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mdsp-packa</b>.
<dt><b>-mEA</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mea</b>.
<dt><b>-mmac_24</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mmac-24</b>.
<dt><b>-mmac_d16</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mmac-d16</b>.
<dt><b>-mspfp_compact</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mspfp-compact</b>.
<dt><b>-mspfp_fast</b>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mspfp-fast</b>.
<dt><b>-mtune=</b><i>cpu</i>
<dd>Values <b>arc600</b>, <b>arc601</b>, <b>arc700</b> and <b>arc700-xmac</b> for <i>cpu</i> are replaced by <font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC600</b></font>, <font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC601</b></font>, <font SIZE="-1"><b>ARC700</b></font> and <b>ARC700-xmac</b> respectively.
<dt><b>-multcost=</b><i>num</i>
<dd>Replaced by <b>-mmultcost</b>.</dl>
 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>ARM</i></font><i> Options</i> 

 These <b>-m</b> options are defined for the <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> port:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-mabi=</b><i>name</i>
<dd>Generate code for the specified <font SIZE="-1">ABI.</font> Permissible values are: <b>apcs-gnu</b>, <b>atpcs</b>, <b>aapcs</b>, <b>aapcs-linux</b> and <b>iwmmxt</b>.
<dt><b>-mapcs-frame</b>
<dd>Generate a stack frame that is compliant with the <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> Procedure Call Standard for all functions, even if this is not strictly necessary for correct execution of the code. Specifying <b>-fomit-frame-pointer</b> with this option causes the stack frames not to be generated for leaf functions. The default is <b>-mno-apcs-frame</b>. This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mapcs</b>
<dd>This is a synonym for <b>-mapcs-frame</b> and is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mthumb-interwork</b>
<dd>Generate code that supports calling between the <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> and Thumb instruction sets. Without this option, on pre-v5 architectures, the two instruction sets cannot be reliably used inside one program. The default is <b>-mno-thumb-interwork</b>, since slightly larger code is generated when <b>-mthumb-interwork</b> is specified. In <font SIZE="-1">AAPCS</font> configurations this option is meaningless.
<dt><b>-mno-sched-prolog</b>
<dd>Prevent the reordering of instructions in the function prologue, or the merging of those instruction with the instructions in the function's body. This means that all functions start with a recognizable set of instructions (or in fact one of a choice from a small set of different function prologues), and this information can be used to locate the start of functions inside an executable piece of code. The default is <b>-msched-prolog</b>.
<dt><b>-mfloat-abi=</b><i>name</i>
<dd>Specifies which floating-point <font SIZE="-1">ABI</font> to use. Permissible values are: <b>soft</b>, <b>softfp</b> and <b>hard</b>. 

 Specifying <b>soft</b> causes <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> to generate output containing library calls for floating-point operations. <b>softfp</b> allows the generation of code using hardware floating-point instructions, but still uses the soft-float calling conventions. <b>hard</b> allows generation of floating-point instructions and uses FPU-specific calling conventions. 

 The default depends on the specific target configuration. Note that the hard-float and soft-float ABIs are not link-compatible; you must compile your entire program with the same <font SIZE="-1">ABI,</font> and link with a compatible set of libraries.
<dt><b>-mgeneral-regs-only</b>
<dd>Generate code which uses only the general-purpose registers. This will prevent the compiler from using floating-point and Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> registers but will not impose any restrictions on the assembler.
<dt><b>-mlittle-endian</b>
<dd>Generate code for a processor running in little-endian mode. This is the default for all standard configurations.
<dt><b>-mbig-endian</b>
<dd>Generate code for a processor running in big-endian mode; the default is to compile code for a little-endian processor.
<dt><b>-mbe8</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mbe32</b>
<dd>When linking a big-endian image select between <font SIZE="-1">BE8</font> and <font SIZE="-1">BE32</font> formats. The option has no effect for little-endian images and is ignored. The default is dependent on the selected target architecture. For ARMv6 and later architectures the default is <font SIZE="-1">BE8,</font> for older architectures the default is <font SIZE="-1">BE32.</font> <font SIZE="-1">BE32</font> format has been deprecated by <font SIZE="-1">ARM.</font>
<dt><b>-march=</b><i>name</i>[<b>+extension...</b>]
<dd>This specifies the name of the target <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> architecture. <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> uses this name to determine what kind of instructions it can emit when generating assembly code. This option can be used in conjunction with or instead of the <b>-mcpu=</b> option. 

 Permissible names are: <b>armv4t</b>, <b>armv5t</b>, <b>armv5te</b>, <b>armv6</b>, <b>armv6j</b>, <b>armv6k</b>, <b>armv6kz</b>, <b>armv6t2</b>, <b>armv6z</b>, <b>armv6zk</b>, <b>armv7</b>, <b>armv7-a</b>, <b>armv7ve</b>, <b>armv8-a</b>, <b>armv8.1-a</b>, <b>armv8.2-a</b>, <b>armv8.3-a</b>, <b>armv8.4-a</b>, <b>armv8.5-a</b>, <b>armv7-r</b>, <b>armv8-r</b>, <b>armv6-m</b>, <b>armv6s-m</b>, <b>armv7-m</b>, <b>armv7e-m</b>, <b>armv8-m.base</b>, <b>armv8-m.main</b>, <b>iwmmxt</b> and <b>iwmmxt2</b>. 

 Additionally, the following architectures, which lack support for the Thumb execution state, are recognized but support is deprecated: <b>armv4</b>. 

 Many of the architectures support extensions. These can be added by appending <b>+</b><i>extension</i> to the architecture name. Extension options are processed in order and capabilities accumulate. An extension will also enable any necessary base extensions upon which it depends. For example, the <b>+crypto</b> extension will always enable the <b>+simd</b> extension. The exception to the additive construction is for extensions that are prefixed with <b>+no...</b>: these extensions disable the specified option and any other extensions that may depend on the presence of that extension. 

 For example, <b>-march=armv7-a+simd+nofp+vfpv4</b> is equivalent to writing <b>-march=armv7-a+vfpv4</b> since the <b>+simd</b> option is entirely disabled by the <b>+nofp</b> option that follows it. 

 Most extension names are generically named, but have an effect that is dependent upon the architecture to which it is applied. For example, the <b>+simd</b> option can be applied to both <b>armv7-a</b> and <b>armv8-a</b> architectures, but will enable the original ARMv7-A Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (Neon) extensions for <b>armv7-a</b> and the ARMv8-A variant for <b>armv8-a</b>. 

 The table below lists the supported extensions for each architecture. Architectures not mentioned do not support any extensions.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>armv5te</b>
<dd><dt><b>armv6</b>
<dd><dt><b>armv6j</b>
<dd><dt><b>armv6k</b>
<dd><dt><b>armv6kz</b>
<dd><dt><b>armv6t2</b>
<dd><dt><b>armv6z</b>
<dd><dt><b>armv6zk</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+fp</b>
<dd>The VFPv2 floating-point instructions. The extension <b>+vfpv2</b> can be used as an alias for this extension.
<dt><b>+nofp</b>
<dd>Disable the floating-point instructions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>armv7</b>
<dd>The common subset of the ARMv7-A, ARMv7-R and ARMv7-M architectures.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+fp</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 16 double-precision registers. The extension <b>+vfpv3-d16</b> can be used as an alias for this extension. Note that floating-point is not supported by the base ARMv7-M architecture, but is compatible with both the ARMv7-A and ARMv7-R architectures.
<dt><b>+nofp</b>
<dd>Disable the floating-point instructions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>armv7-a</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+mp</b>
<dd>The multiprocessing extension.
<dt><b>+sec</b>
<dd>The security extension.
<dt><b>+fp</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 16 double-precision registers. The extension <b>+vfpv3-d16</b> can be used as an alias for this extension.
<dt><b>+simd</b>
<dd>The Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (Neon) v1 and the VFPv3 floating-point instructions. The extensions <b>+neon</b> and <b>+neon-vfpv3</b> can be used as aliases for this extension.
<dt><b>+vfpv3</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 32 double-precision registers.
<dt><b>+vfpv3-d16-fp16</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 16 double-precision registers and the half-precision floating-point conversion operations.
<dt><b>+vfpv3-fp16</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 32 double-precision registers and the half-precision floating-point conversion operations.
<dt><b>+vfpv4-d16</b>
<dd>The VFPv4 floating-point instructions, with 16 double-precision registers.
<dt><b>+vfpv4</b>
<dd>The VFPv4 floating-point instructions, with 32 double-precision registers.
<dt><b>+neon-fp16</b>
<dd>The Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (Neon) v1 and the VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with the half-precision floating-point conversion operations.
<dt><b>+neon-vfpv4</b>
<dd>The Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (Neon) v2 and the VFPv4 floating-point instructions.
<dt><b>+nosimd</b>
<dd>Disable the Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> instructions (does not disable floating point).
<dt><b>+nofp</b>
<dd>Disable the floating-point and Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> instructions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>armv7ve</b>
<dd>The extended version of the ARMv7-A architecture with support for virtualization.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+fp</b>
<dd>The VFPv4 floating-point instructions, with 16 double-precision registers. The extension <b>+vfpv4-d16</b> can be used as an alias for this extension.
<dt><b>+simd</b>
<dd>The Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (Neon) v2 and the VFPv4 floating-point instructions. The extension <b>+neon-vfpv4</b> can be used as an alias for this extension.
<dt><b>+vfpv3-d16</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 16 double-precision registers.
<dt><b>+vfpv3</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 32 double-precision registers.
<dt><b>+vfpv3-d16-fp16</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 16 double-precision registers and the half-precision floating-point conversion operations.
<dt><b>+vfpv3-fp16</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with 32 double-precision registers and the half-precision floating-point conversion operations.
<dt><b>+vfpv4-d16</b>
<dd>The VFPv4 floating-point instructions, with 16 double-precision registers.
<dt><b>+vfpv4</b>
<dd>The VFPv4 floating-point instructions, with 32 double-precision registers.
<dt><b>+neon</b>
<dd>The Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (Neon) v1 and the VFPv3 floating-point instructions. The extension <b>+neon-vfpv3</b> can be used as an alias for this extension.
<dt><b>+neon-fp16</b>
<dd>The Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (Neon) v1 and the VFPv3 floating-point instructions, with the half-precision floating-point conversion operations.
<dt><b>+nosimd</b>
<dd>Disable the Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> instructions (does not disable floating point).
<dt><b>+nofp</b>
<dd>Disable the floating-point and Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> instructions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>armv8-a</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+crc</b>
<dd>The Cyclic Redundancy Check (<font SIZE="-1">CRC</font>) instructions.
<dt><b>+simd</b>
<dd>The ARMv8-A Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions.
<dt><b>+crypto</b>
<dd>The cryptographic instructions.
<dt><b>+nocrypto</b>
<dd>Disable the cryptographic instructions.
<dt><b>+nofp</b>
<dd>Disable the floating-point, Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and cryptographic instructions.
<dt><b>+sb</b>
<dd>Speculation Barrier Instruction.
<dt><b>+predres</b>
<dd>Execution and Data Prediction Restriction Instructions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>armv8.1-a</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+simd</b>
<dd>The ARMv8.1-A Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions.
<dt><b>+crypto</b>
<dd>The cryptographic instructions. This also enables the Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions.
<dt><b>+nocrypto</b>
<dd>Disable the cryptographic instructions.
<dt><b>+nofp</b>
<dd>Disable the floating-point, Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and cryptographic instructions.
<dt><b>+sb</b>
<dd>Speculation Barrier Instruction.
<dt><b>+predres</b>
<dd>Execution and Data Prediction Restriction Instructions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>armv8.2-a</b>
<dd><dt><b>armv8.3-a</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+fp16</b>
<dd>The half-precision floating-point data processing instructions. This also enables the Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions.
<dt><b>+fp16fml</b>
<dd>The half-precision floating-point fmla extension. This also enables the half-precision floating-point extension and Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions.
<dt><b>+simd</b>
<dd>The ARMv8.1-A Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions.
<dt><b>+crypto</b>
<dd>The cryptographic instructions. This also enables the Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions.
<dt><b>+dotprod</b>
<dd>Enable the Dot Product extension. This also enables Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> instructions.
<dt><b>+nocrypto</b>

<dt><b>+sb</b>
<dd>Speculation Barrier Instruction.
<dt><b>+predres</b>
<dd>Execution and Data Prediction Restriction Instructions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>armv8.4-a</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+fp16</b>
<dd>The half-precision floating-point data processing instructions. This also enables the Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions as well as the Dot Product extension and the half-precision floating-point fmla extension.

<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+fp16</b>
<dd>The half-precision floating-point data processing instructions. This also enables the Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions as well as the Dot Product extension and the half-precision floating-point fmla extension.
<dt><b>+simd</b>
<dd>The ARMv8.3-A Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions as well as the Dot Product extension.

<dd>Disable the floating-point, Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and cryptographic instructions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>armv7-r</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+fp.sp</b>
<dd>The single-precision VFPv3 floating-point instructions. The extension <b>+vfpv3xd</b> can be used as an alias for this extension.
<dt><b>+fp</b>
<dd>The VFPv3 floating-point instructions with 16 double-precision registers. The extension +vfpv3-d16 can be used as an alias for this extension.
<dt><b>+vfpv3xd-d16-fp16</b>
<dd>The single-precision VFPv3 floating-point instructions with 16 double-precision registers and the half-precision floating-point conversion operations.
<dt><b>+vfpv3-d16-fp16</b>

<dt><b>+nofp</b>

<dt><b>+noidiv</b>

<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+fp</b>
<dd>The single-precision VFPv4 floating-point instructions.

<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+dsp</b>
<dd>The <font SIZE="-1">DSP</font> instructions.
<dt><b>+nodsp</b>
<dd>Disable the <font SIZE="-1">DSP</font> extension.
<dt><b>+fp</b>

<dd>The Cyclic Redundancy Check (<font SIZE="-1">CRC</font>) instructions.

</dl><dl COMPACT><dd><b>-march=native</b> causes the compiler to auto-detect the architecture of the build computer. At present, this feature is only supported on GNU/Linux, and not all architectures are recognized. If the auto-detect is unsuccessful the option has no effect.</dl><dt><b>-mtune=</b><i>name</i>
<dd>This option specifies the name of the target <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> processor for which <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> should tune the performance of the code. For some <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> implementations better performance can be obtained by using this option. Permissible names are: <b>arm7tdmi</b>, <b>arm7tdmi-s</b>, <b>arm710t</b>, <b>arm720t</b>, <b>arm740t</b>, <b>strongarm</b>, <b>strongarm110</b>, <b>strongarm1100</b>, 0<b>strongarm1110</b>, <b>arm8</b>, <b>arm810</b>, <b>arm9</b>, <b>arm9e</b>, <b>arm920</b>, <b>arm920t</b>, <b>arm922t</b>, <b>arm946e-s</b>, <b>arm966e-s</b>, <b>arm968e-s</b>, <b>arm926ej-s</b>, <b>arm940t</b>, <b>arm9tdmi</b>, <b>arm10tdmi</b>, <b>arm1020t</b>, <b>arm1026ej-s</b>, <b>arm10e</b>, <b>arm1020e</b>, <b>arm1022e</b>, <b>arm1136j-s</b>, <b>arm1136jf-s</b>, <b>mpcore</b>, <b>mpcorenovfp</b>, <b>arm1156t2-s</b>, <b>arm1156t2f-s</b>, <b>arm1176jz-s</b>, <b>arm1176jzf-s</b>, <b>generic-armv7-a</b>, <b>cortex-a5</b>, <b>cortex-a7</b>, <b>cortex-a8</b>, <b>cortex-a9</b>, <b>cortex-a12</b>, <b>cortex-a15</b>, <b>cortex-a17</b>, <b>cortex-a32</b>, <b>cortex-a35</b>, <b>cortex-a53</b>, <b>cortex-a55</b>, <b>cortex-a57</b>, <b>cortex-a72</b>, <b>cortex-a73</b>, <b>cortex-a75</b>, <b>cortex-a76</b>, <b>ares</b>, <b>cortex-r4</b>, <b>cortex-r4f</b>, <b>cortex-r5</b>, <b>cortex-r7</b>, <b>cortex-r8</b>, <b>cortex-r52</b>, <b>cortex-m0</b>, <b>cortex-m0plus</b>, <b>cortex-m1</b>, <b>cortex-m3</b>, <b>cortex-m4</b>, <b>cortex-m7</b>, <b>cortex-m23</b>, <b>cortex-m33</b>, <b>cortex-m1.small-multiply</b>, <b>cortex-m0.small-multiply</b>, <b>cortex-m0plus.small-multiply</b>, <b>exynos-m1</b>, <b>marvell-pj4</b>, <b>neoverse-n1</b>, <b>neoverse-n2</b>, <b>neoverse-v1</b>, <b>xscale</b>, <b>iwmmxt</b>, <b>iwmmxt2</b>, <b>ep9312</b>, <b>fa526</b>, <b>fa626</b>, <b>fa606te</b>, <b>fa626te</b>, <b>fmp626</b>, <b>fa726te</b>, <b>xgene1</b>. 

 Additionally, this option can specify that <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> should tune the performance of the code for a big.LITTLE system. Permissible names are: <b>cortex-a15.cortex-a7</b>, <b>cortex-a17.cortex-a7</b>, <b>cortex-a57.cortex-a53</b>, <b>cortex-a72.cortex-a53</b>, <b>cortex-a72.cortex-a35</b>, <b>cortex-a73.cortex-a53</b>, <b>cortex-a75.cortex-a55</b>, <b>cortex-a76.cortex-a55</b>. 

 <b>-mtune=generic-</b><i>arch</i> specifies that <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> should tune the performance for a blend of processors within architecture <i>arch</i>. The aim is to generate code that run well on the current most popular processors, balancing between optimizations that benefit some CPUs in the range, and avoiding performance pitfalls of other CPUs. The effects of this option may change in future <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> versions as <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> models come and go. 

 <b>-mtune</b> permits the same extension options as <b>-mcpu</b>, but the extension options do not affect the tuning of the generated code. 

 <b>-mtune=native</b> causes the compiler to auto-detect the <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> of the build computer. At present, this feature is only supported on GNU/Linux, and not all architectures are recognized. If the auto-detect is unsuccessful the option has no effect.
<dt><b>-mcpu=</b><i>name</i>[<b>+extension...</b>]
<dd>This specifies the name of the target <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> processor. <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> uses this name to derive the name of the target <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> architecture (as if specified by <b>-march</b>) and the <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> processor type for which to tune for performance (as if specified by <b>-mtune</b>). Where this option is used in conjunction with <b>-march</b> or <b>-mtune</b>, those options take precedence over the appropriate part of this option. 

 Many of the supported CPUs implement optional architectural extensions. Where this is so the architectural extensions are normally enabled by default. If implementations that lack the extension exist, then the extension syntax can be used to disable those extensions that have been omitted. For floating-point and Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (Neon) instructions, the settings of the options <b>-mfloat-abi</b> and <b>-mfpu</b> must also be considered: floating-point and Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> instructions will only be used if <b>-mfloat-abi</b> is not set to <b>soft</b>; and any setting of <b>-mfpu</b> other than <b>auto</b> will override the available floating-point and <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> extension instructions. 

 For example, <b>cortex-a9</b> can be found in three major configurations: integer only, with just a floating-point unit or with floating-point and Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD.</font> The default is to enable all the instructions, but the extensions <b>+nosimd</b> and <b>+nofp</b> can be used to disable just the <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> or both the <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> and floating-point instructions respectively. 

 Permissible names for this option are the same as those for <b>-mtune</b>. 

 The following extension options are common to the listed CPUs:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>+nodsp</b>
<dd>Disable the <font SIZE="-1">DSP</font> instructions on <b>cortex-m33</b>.
<dt><b>+nofp</b>
<dd>Disables the floating-point instructions on <b>arm9e</b>, <b>arm946e-s</b>, <b>arm966e-s</b>, <b>arm968e-s</b>, <b>arm10e</b>, <b>arm1020e</b>, <b>arm1022e</b>, <b>arm926ej-s</b>, <b>arm1026ej-s</b>, <b>cortex-r5</b>, <b>cortex-r7</b>, <b>cortex-r8</b>, <b>cortex-m4</b>, <b>cortex-m7</b> and <b>cortex-m33</b>. Disables the floating-point and <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> instructions on <b>generic-armv7-a</b>, <b>cortex-a5</b>, <b>cortex-a7</b>, <b>cortex-a8</b>, <b>cortex-a9</b>, <b>cortex-a12</b>, <b>cortex-a15</b>, <b>cortex-a17</b>, <b>cortex-a15.cortex-a7</b>, <b>cortex-a17.cortex-a7</b>, <b>cortex-a32</b>, <b>cortex-a35</b>, <b>cortex-a53</b> and <b>cortex-a55</b>.
<dt><b>+nofp.dp</b>
<dd>Disables the double-precision component of the floating-point instructions on <b>cortex-r5</b>, <b>cortex-r7</b>, <b>cortex-r8</b>, <b>cortex-r52</b> and <b>cortex-m7</b>.
<dt><b>+nosimd</b>
<dd>Disables the <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> (but not floating-point) instructions on <b>generic-armv7-a</b>, <b>cortex-a5</b>, <b>cortex-a7</b> and <b>cortex-a9</b>.
<dt><b>+crypto</b>
<dd>Enables the cryptographic instructions on <b>cortex-a32</b>, <b>cortex-a35</b>, <b>cortex-a53</b>, <b>cortex-a55</b>, <b>cortex-a57</b>, <b>cortex-a72</b>, <b>cortex-a73</b>, <b>cortex-a75</b>, <b>exynos-m1</b>, <b>xgene1</b>, <b>cortex-a57.cortex-a53</b>, <b>cortex-a72.cortex-a53</b>, <b>cortex-a73.cortex-a35</b>, <b>cortex-a73.cortex-a53</b> and <b>cortex-a75.cortex-a55</b>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Additionally the <b>generic-armv7-a</b> pseudo target defaults to VFPv3 with 16 double-precision registers. It supports the following extension options: <b>mp</b>, <b>sec</b>, <b>vfpv3-d16</b>, <b>vfpv3</b>, <b>vfpv3-d16-fp16</b>, <b>vfpv3-fp16</b>, <b>vfpv4-d16</b>, <b>vfpv4</b>, <b>neon</b>, <b>neon-vfpv3</b>, <b>neon-fp16</b>, <b>neon-vfpv4</b>. The meanings are the same as for the extensions to <b>-march=armv7-a</b>. 

 <b>-mcpu=generic-</b><i>arch</i> is also permissible, and is equivalent to <b>-march=</b><i>arch</i> <b>-mtune=generic-</b><i>arch</i>. See <b>-mtune</b> for more information. 

 <b>-mcpu=native</b> causes the compiler to auto-detect the <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> of the build computer. At present, this feature is only supported on GNU/Linux, and not all architectures are recognized. If the auto-detect is unsuccessful the option has no effect.</dl><dt><b>-mfpu=</b><i>name</i>
<dd>This specifies what floating-point hardware (or hardware emulation) is available on the target. Permissible names are: <b>auto</b>, <b>vfpv2</b>, <b>vfpv3</b>, <b>vfpv3-fp16</b>, <b>vfpv3-d16</b>, <b>vfpv3-d16-fp16</b>, <b>vfpv3xd</b>, <b>vfpv3xd-fp16</b>, <b>neon-vfpv3</b>, <b>neon-fp16</b>, <b>vfpv4</b>, <b>vfpv4-d16</b>, <b>fpv4-sp-d16</b>, <b>neon-vfpv4</b>, <b>fpv5-d16</b>, <b>fpv5-sp-d16</b>, <b>fp-armv8</b>, <b>neon-fp-armv8</b> and <b>crypto-neon-fp-armv8</b>. Note that <b>neon</b> is an alias for <b>neon-vfpv3</b> and <b>vfp</b> is an alias for <b>vfpv2</b>. 

 The setting <b>auto</b> is the default and is special. It causes the compiler to select the floating-point and Advanced <font SIZE="-1">SIMD</font> instructions based on the settings of <b>-mcpu</b> and <b>-march</b>. 

 If the selected floating-point hardware includes the <font SIZE="-1">NEON</font> extension (e.g. <b>-mfpu=neon</b>), note that floating-point operations are not generated by <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font>'s auto-vectorization pass unless <b>-funsafe-math-optimizations</b> is also specified. This is because <font SIZE="-1">NEON</font> hardware does not fully implement the <font SIZE="-1">IEEE 754</font> standard for floating-point arithmetic (in particular denormal values are treated as zero), so the use of <font SIZE="-1">NEON</font> instructions may lead to a loss of precision. 

 You can also set the fpu name at function level by using the <tt>&quot;target(&quot;fpu=&quot;)&quot;</tt> function attributes or pragmas.
<dt><b>-mfp16-format=</b><i>name</i>
<dd>Specify the format of the <tt>&quot;__fp16&quot;</tt> half-precision floating-point type. Permissible names are <b>none</b>, <b>ieee</b>, and <b>alternative</b>; the default is <b>none</b>, in which case the <tt>&quot;__fp16&quot;</tt> type is not defined.
<dt><b>-mstructure-size-boundary=</b><i>n</i>
<dd>The sizes of all structures and unions are rounded up to a multiple of the number of bits set by this option. Permissible values are 8, 32 and 64. The default value varies for different toolchains. For the <font SIZE="-1">COFF</font> targeted toolchain the default value is 8. A value of 64 is only allowed if the underlying <font SIZE="-1">ABI</font> supports it. 

 Specifying a larger number can produce faster, more efficient code, but can also increase the size of the program. Different values are potentially incompatible. Code compiled with one value cannot necessarily expect to work with code or libraries compiled with another value, if they exchange information using structures or unions. 

 This option is deprecated.
<dt><b>-mabort-on-noreturn</b>
<dd>Generate a call to the function <tt>&quot;abort&quot;</tt> at the end of a <tt>&quot;noreturn&quot;</tt> function. It is executed if the function tries to return.
<dt><b>-mlong-calls</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mno-long-calls</b>
<dd>Tells the compiler to perform function calls by first loading the address of the function into a register and then performing a subroutine call on this register. This switch is needed if the target function lies outside of the 64-megabyte addressing range of the offset-based version of subroutine call instruction. 

 Even if this switch is enabled, not all function calls are turned into long calls. The heuristic is that static functions, functions that have the <tt>&quot;short_call&quot;</tt> attribute, functions that are inside the scope of a <tt>&quot;#pragma no_long_calls&quot;</tt> directive, and functions whose definitions have already been compiled within the current compilation unit are not turned into long calls. The exceptions to this rule are that weak function definitions, functions with the <tt>&quot;long_call&quot;</tt> attribute or the <tt>&quot;section&quot;</tt> attribute, and functions that are within the scope of a <tt>&quot;#pragma long_calls&quot;</tt> directive are always turned into long calls. 

 This feature is not enabled by default. Specifying <b>-mno-long-calls</b> restores the default behavior, as does placing the function calls within the scope of a <tt>&quot;#pragma long_calls_off&quot;</tt> directive. Note these switches have no effect on how the compiler generates code to handle function calls via function pointers.
<dt><b>-msingle-pic-base</b>
<dd>Treat the register used for <font SIZE="-1">PIC</font> addressing as read-only, rather than loading it in the prologue for each function. The runtime system is responsible for initializing this register with an appropriate value before execution begins.
<dt><b>-mpic-register=</b><i>reg</i>
<dd>Specify the register to be used for <font SIZE="-1">PIC</font> addressing. For standard <font SIZE="-1">PIC</font> base case, the default is any suitable register determined by compiler. For single <font SIZE="-1">PIC</font> base case, the default is <b>R9</b> if target is <font SIZE="-1">EABI</font> based or stack-checking is enabled, otherwise the default is <b>R10</b>.
<dt><b>-mpic-data-is-text-relative</b>
<dd>Assume that the displacement between the text and data segments is fixed at static link time. This permits using PC-relative addressing operations to access data known to be in the data segment. For non-VxWorks <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> targets, this option is enabled by default. When disabled on such targets, it will enable <b>-msingle-pic-base</b> by default.
<dt><b>-mpoke-function-name</b>
<dd>Write the name of each function into the text section, directly preceding the function prologue. The generated code is similar to this: 

 <pre> t0
 .ascii &quot;arm_poke_function_name&quot;, 0
 .align
 t1
 .word 0xff000000 + (t1 - t0)
 arm_poke_function_name
 mov ip, sp
 stmfd sp!, {fp, ip, lr, pc}
 sub fp, ip, #4</pre>When performing a stack backtrace, code can inspect the value of <tt>&quot;pc&quot;</tt> stored at <tt>&quot;fp + 0&quot;</tt>. If the trace function then looks at location <tt>&quot;pc - 12&quot;</tt> and the top 8 bits are set, then we know that there is a function name embedded immediately preceding this location and has length <tt>&quot;((pc[-3]) &amp; 0xff000000)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>-mthumb</b>
<dd><dt><b>-marm</b>
<dd>Select between generating code that executes in <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> and Thumb states. The default for most configurations is to generate code that executes in <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> state, but the default can be changed by configuring <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> with the <b>--with-mode=</b><i>state</i> configure option. 

 You can also override the <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> and Thumb mode for each function by using the <tt>&quot;target(&quot;thumb&quot;)&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;target(&quot;arm&quot;)&quot;</tt> function attributes or pragmas.
<dt><b>-mflip-thumb</b>
<dd>Switch ARM/Thumb modes on alternating functions. This option is provided for regression testing of mixed Thumb/ARM code generation, and is not intended for ordinary use in compiling code.
<dt><b>-mtpcs-frame</b>
<dd>Generate a stack frame that is compliant with the Thumb Procedure Call Standard for all non-leaf functions. (A leaf function is one that does not call any other functions.) The default is <b>-mno-tpcs-frame</b>.
<dt><b>-mtpcs-leaf-frame</b>
<dd>Generate a stack frame that is compliant with the Thumb Procedure Call Standard for all leaf functions. (A leaf function is one that does not call any other functions.) The default is <b>-mno-apcs-leaf-frame</b>.
<dt><b>-mcallee-super-interworking</b>
<dd>Gives all externally visible functions in the file being compiled an <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> instruction set header which switches to Thumb mode before executing the rest of the function. This allows these functions to be called from non-interworking code. This option is not valid in <font SIZE="-1">AAPCS</font> configurations because interworking is enabled by default.
<dt><b>-mcaller-super-interworking</b>
<dd>Allows calls via function pointers (including virtual functions) to execute correctly regardless of whether the target code has been compiled for interworking or not. There is a small overhead in the cost of executing a function pointer if this option is enabled. This option is not valid in <font SIZE="-1">AAPCS</font> configurations because interworking is enabled by default.
<dt><b>-mtp=</b><i>name</i>
<dd>Specify the access model for the thread local storage pointer. The valid models are <b>soft</b>, which generates calls to <tt>&quot;__aeabi_read_tp&quot;</tt>, <b>cp15</b>, which fetches the thread pointer from <tt>&quot;cp15&quot;</tt> directly (supported in the arm6k architecture), and <b>auto</b>, which uses the best available method for the selected processor. The default setting is <b>auto</b>.
<dt><b>-mtls-dialect=</b><i>dialect</i>
<dd>Specify the dialect to use for accessing thread local storage. Two <i>dialect</i>s are supported---<b>gnu</b> and <b>gnu2</b>. The <b>gnu</b> dialect selects the original <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> scheme for supporting local and global dynamic <font SIZE="-1">TLS</font> models. The <b>gnu2</b> dialect selects the <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> descriptor scheme, which provides better performance for shared libraries. The <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> descriptor scheme is compatible with the original scheme, but does require new assembler, linker and library support. Initial and local exec <font SIZE="-1">TLS</font> models are unaffected by this option and always use the original scheme.
<dt><b>-mword-relocations</b>
<dd>Only generate absolute relocations on word-sized values (i.e. R_ARM_ABS32). This is enabled by default on targets (uClinux, SymbianOS) where the runtime loader imposes this restriction, and when <b>-fpic</b> or <b>-fPIC</b> is specified. This option conflicts with <b>-mslow-flash-data</b>.
<dt><b>-mfix-cortex-m3-ldrd</b>
<dd>Some Cortex-M3 cores can cause data corruption when <tt>&quot;ldrd&quot;</tt> instructions with overlapping destination and base registers are used. This option avoids generating these instructions. This option is enabled by default when <b>-mcpu=cortex-m3</b> is specified.
<dt><b>-munaligned-access</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mno-unaligned-access</b>
<dd>Enables (or disables) reading and writing of 16- and 32- bit values from addresses that are not 16- or 32- bit aligned. By default unaligned access is disabled for all pre-ARMv6, all ARMv6-M and for ARMv8-M Baseline architectures, and enabled for all other architectures. If unaligned access is not enabled then words in packed data structures are accessed a byte at a time. 

 The <font SIZE="-1">ARM</font> attribute <tt>&quot;Tag_CPU_unaligned_access&quot;</tt> is set in the generated object file to either true or false, depending upon the setting of this option. If unaligned access is enabled then the preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__ARM_FEATURE_UNALIGNED&quot;</tt> is also defined.
<dt><b>-mneon-for-64bits</b>
<dd>Enables using Neon to handle scalar 64-bits operations. This is disabled by default since the cost of moving data from core registers to Neon is high.
<dt><b>-mslow-flash-data</b>
<dd>Assume loading data from flash is slower than fetching instruction. Therefore literal load is minimized for better performance. This option is only supported when compiling for ARMv7 M-profile and off by default. It conflicts with <b>-mword-relocations</b>.
<dt><b>-masm-syntax-unified</b>
<dd>Assume inline assembler is using unified asm syntax. The default is currently off which implies divided syntax. This option has no impact on Thumb2. However, this may change in future releases of <font SIZE="-1">GCC.</font> Divided syntax should be considered deprecated.
<dt><b>-mrestrict-it</b>
<dd>Restricts generation of <font SIZE="-1">IT</font> blocks to conform to the rules of ARMv8-A. <font SIZE="-1">IT</font> blocks can only contain a single 16-bit instruction from a select set of instructions. This option is on by default for ARMv8-A Thumb mode.
<dt><b>-mprint-tune-info</b>
<dd>Print <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> tuning information as comment in assembler file. This is an option used only for regression testing of the compiler and not intended for ordinary use in compiling code. This option is disabled by default.
<dt><b>-mverbose-cost-dump</b>
<dd>Enable verbose cost model dumping in the debug dump files. This option is provided for use in debugging the compiler.
<dt><b>-mpure-code</b>
<dd>Do not allow constant data to be placed in code sections. Additionally, when compiling for <font SIZE="-1">ELF</font> object format give all text sections the <font SIZE="-1">ELF</font> processor-specific section attribute <tt>&quot;SHF_ARM_PURECODE&quot;</tt>. This option is only available when generating non-pic code for M-profile targets.
<dt><b>-mcmse</b>
<dd>Generate secure code as per the ``ARMv8-M Security Extensions: Requirements on Development Tools Engineering Specification'', which can be found on &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://developer.arm.com/documentation/ecm0359818/latest/">https://developer.arm.com/documentation/ecm0359818/latest/</a></b>&gt;.</dl>
 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AVR</i></font><i> Options</i> 

 These options are defined for <font SIZE="-1">AVR</font> implementations:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-mmcu=</b><i>mcu</i>
<dd>Specify Atmel <font SIZE="-1">AVR</font> instruction set architectures (<font SIZE="-1">ISA</font>) or <font SIZE="-1">MCU</font> type. 

 The default for this option is <b>avr2</b>. 

 <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> supports the following <font SIZE="-1">AVR</font> devices and ISAs:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&quot;avr2&quot;
<dd>``Classic'' devices with up to 8 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;attiny22&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny26&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s2313&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s2323&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s2333&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s2343&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s4414&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s4433&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s4434&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90c8534&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s8515&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s8535&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr25&quot;
<dd>``Classic'' devices with up to 8 KiB of program memory and with the <tt>&quot;MOVW&quot;</tt> instruction. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;attiny13&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny13a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny24&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny24a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny25&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny261&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny261a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny2313&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny2313a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny43u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny44&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny44a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny45&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny48&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny441&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny461&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny461a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny4313&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny84&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny84a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny85&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny87&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny88&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny828&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny841&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny861&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny861a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5272&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata6616c&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at86rf401&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr3&quot;
<dd>``Classic'' devices with 16 KiB up to 64 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;at76c711&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at43usb355&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr31&quot;
<dd>``Classic'' devices with 128 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atmega103&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at43usb320&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr35&quot;
<dd>``Classic'' devices with 16 KiB up to 64 KiB of program memory and with the <tt>&quot;MOVW&quot;</tt> instruction. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;attiny167&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny1634&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega8u2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega16u2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32u2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5505&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata6617c&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata664251&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90usb82&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90usb162&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr4&quot;
<dd>``Enhanced'' devices with up to 8 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atmega48&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega48a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega48p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega48pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega48pb&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega8&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega8a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega8hva&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega88&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega88a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega88p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega88pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega88pb&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega8515&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega8535&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata6285&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata6286&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata6289&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata6612c&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm2b&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm3b&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm81&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr5&quot;
<dd>``Enhanced'' devices with 16 KiB up to 64 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atmega16&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega16a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega16hva&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega16hva2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega16hvb&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega16hvbrevb&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega16m1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega16u4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega161&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega162&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega163&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega164a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega164p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega164pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega165&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega165a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega165p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega165pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega168&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega168a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega168p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega168pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega168pb&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega169&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega169a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega169p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega169pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32c1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32hvb&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32hvbrevb&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32m1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32u4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega32u6&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega323&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega324a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega324p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega324pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega325&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega325a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega325p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega325pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega328&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega328p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega328pb&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega329&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega329a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega329p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega329pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3250&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3250a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3250p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3250pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3290&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3290a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3290p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3290pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega406&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega64&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega64a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega64c1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega64hve&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega64hve2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega64m1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega64rfr2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega640&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega644&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega644a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega644p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega644pa&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega644rfr2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega645&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega645a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega645p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega649&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega649a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega649p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega6450&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega6450a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega6450p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega6490&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega6490a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega6490p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5795&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5790&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5790n&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5791&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata6613c&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata6614q&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5782&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5831&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata8210&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata8510&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;ata5702m322&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm161&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm216&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90pwm316&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90can32&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90can64&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90scr100&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90usb646&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90usb647&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at94k&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;m3000&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr51&quot;
<dd>``Enhanced'' devices with 128 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atmega128&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega128a&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega128rfa1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega128rfr2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega1280&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega1281&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega1284&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega1284p&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega1284rfr2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90can128&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90usb1286&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90usb1287&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr6&quot;
<dd>``Enhanced'' devices with 3-byte <font SIZE="-1">PC,</font> i.e. with more than 128 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atmega256rfr2&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega2560&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega2561&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega2564rfr2&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avrxmega2&quot;
<dd>``<font SIZE="-1">XMEGA''</font> devices with more than 8 KiB and up to 64 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atxmega8e5&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega16a4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega16a4u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega16c4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega16d4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega16e5&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega32a4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega32a4u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega32c3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega32c4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega32d3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega32d4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega32e5&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avrxmega3&quot;
<dd>``<font SIZE="-1">XMEGA''</font> devices with up to 64 KiB of combined program memory and <font SIZE="-1">RAM,</font> and with program memory visible in the <font SIZE="-1">RAM</font> address space. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;attiny202&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny204&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny212&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny214&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny402&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny404&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny406&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny412&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny414&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny416&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny417&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny804&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny806&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny807&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny814&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny816&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny817&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny1604&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny1606&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny1607&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny1614&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny1616&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny1617&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny3214&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny3216&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny3217&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega808&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega809&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega1608&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega1609&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3208&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega3209&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega4808&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atmega4809&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avrxmega4&quot;
<dd>``<font SIZE="-1">XMEGA''</font> devices with more than 64 KiB and up to 128 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atxmega64a3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega64a3u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega64a4u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega64b1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega64b3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega64c3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega64d3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega64d4&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avrxmega5&quot;
<dd>``<font SIZE="-1">XMEGA''</font> devices with more than 64 KiB and up to 128 KiB of program memory and more than 64 KiB of <font SIZE="-1">RAM.</font> <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atxmega64a1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega64a1u&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avrxmega6&quot;
<dd>``<font SIZE="-1">XMEGA''</font> devices with more than 128 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atxmega128a3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega128a3u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega128b1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega128b3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega128c3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega128d3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega128d4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega192a3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega192a3u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega192c3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega192d3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega256a3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega256a3b&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega256a3bu&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega256a3u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega256c3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega256d3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega384c3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega384d3&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avrxmega7&quot;
<dd>``<font SIZE="-1">XMEGA''</font> devices with more than 128 KiB of program memory and more than 64 KiB of <font SIZE="-1">RAM.</font> <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;atxmega128a1&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega128a1u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;atxmega128a4u&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avrtiny&quot;
<dd>``<font SIZE="-1">TINY''</font> Tiny core devices with 512 B up to 4 KiB of program memory. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;attiny4&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny5&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny9&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny10&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny20&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny40&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&quot;avr1&quot;
<dd>This <font SIZE="-1">ISA</font> is implemented by the minimal <font SIZE="-1">AVR</font> core and supported for assembler only. <i>mcu</i> = <tt>&quot;attiny11&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny12&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny15&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;attiny28&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;at90s1200&quot;</tt>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-mabsdata</b>
<dd>Assume that all data in static storage can be accessed by <font SIZE="-1">LDS / STS</font> instructions. This option has only an effect on reduced Tiny devices like ATtiny40. See also the <tt>&quot;absdata&quot;</tt> <font SIZE="-1"><b>AVR</b></font><b> Variable Attributes,variable attribute</b>.
<dt><b>-maccumulate-args</b>
<dd>Accumulate outgoing function arguments and acquire/release the needed stack space for outgoing function arguments once in function prologue/epilogue. Without this option, outgoing arguments are pushed before calling a function and popped afterwards. 

 Popping the arguments after the function call can be expensive on <font SIZE="-1">AVR</font> so that accumulating the stack space might lead to smaller executables because arguments need not be removed from the stack after such a function call. 

 This option can lead to reduced code size for functions that perform several calls to functions that get their arguments on the stack like calls to printf-like functions.
<dt><b>-mbranch-cost=</b><i>cost</i>
<dd>Set the branch costs for conditional branch instructions to <i>cost</i>. Reasonable values for <i>cost</i> are small, non-negative integers. The default branch cost is 0.
<dt><b>-mcall-prologues</b>
<dd>Functions prologues/epilogues are expanded as calls to appropriate subroutines. Code size is smaller.
<dt><b>-mgas-isr-prologues</b>
<dd>Interrupt service routines (ISRs) may use the <tt>&quot;__gcc_isr&quot;</tt> pseudo instruction supported by <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> Binutils. If this option is on, the feature can still be disabled for individual ISRs by means of the <font SIZE="-1"><b>AVR</b></font><b> Function Attributes,,</b>&quot;no_gccisr&quot; function attribute. This feature is activated per default if optimization is on (but not with <b>-Og</b>, <tt>@pxref</tt>{Optimize Options}), and if <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> Binutils support <font SIZE="-1">PR21683</font> (<tt>&quot;<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://sourceware.org/PR21683">https://sourceware.org/PR21683</a>&quot;</tt>).
<dt><b>-mint8</b>
<dd>Assume <tt>&quot;int&quot;</tt> to be 8-bit integer. This affects the sizes of all types: a <tt>&quot;char&quot;</tt> is 1 byte, an <tt>&quot;int&quot;</tt> is 1 byte, a <tt>&quot;long&quot;</tt> is 2 bytes, and <tt>&quot;long long&quot;</tt> is 4 bytes. Please note that this option does not conform to the C standards, but it results in smaller code size.
<dt><b>-mmain-is-OS_task</b>
<dd>Do not save registers in <tt>&quot;main&quot;</tt>. The effect is the same like attaching attribute <font SIZE="-1"><b>AVR</b></font><b> Function Attributes,,</b>&quot;OS_task&quot; to <tt>&quot;main&quot;</tt>. It is activated per default if optimization is on.
<dt><b>-mn-flash=</b><i>num</i>
<dd>Assume that the flash memory has a size of <i>num</i> times 64 KiB.
<dt><b>-mno-interrupts</b>
<dd>Generated code is not compatible with hardware interrupts. Code size is smaller.
<dt><b>-mrelax</b>
<dd>Try to replace <tt>&quot;CALL&quot;</tt> resp. <tt>&quot;JMP&quot;</tt> instruction by the shorter <tt>&quot;RCALL&quot;</tt> resp. <tt>&quot;RJMP&quot;</tt> instruction if applicable. Setting <b>-mrelax</b> just adds the <b>--mlink-relax</b> option to the assembler's command line and the <b>--relax</b> option to the linker's command line. 

 Jump relaxing is performed by the linker because jump offsets are not known before code is located. Therefore, the assembler code generated by the compiler is the same, but the instructions in the executable may differ from instructions in the assembler code. 

 Relaxing must be turned on if linker stubs are needed, see the section on <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> and linker stubs below.
<dt><b>-mrmw</b>
<dd>Assume that the device supports the Read-Modify-Write instructions <tt>&quot;XCH&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;LAC&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;LAS&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;LAT&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>-mshort-calls</b>
<dd>Assume that <tt>&quot;RJMP&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;RCALL&quot;</tt> can target the whole program memory. 

 This option is used internally for multilib selection. It is not an optimization option, and you don't need to set it by hand.
<dt><b>-msp8</b>
<dd>Treat the stack pointer register as an 8-bit register, i.e. assume the high byte of the stack pointer is zero. In general, you don't need to set this option by hand. 

 This option is used internally by the compiler to select and build multilibs for architectures <tt>&quot;avr2&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;avr25&quot;</tt>. These architectures mix devices with and without <tt>&quot;SPH&quot;</tt>. For any setting other than <b>-mmcu=avr2</b> or <b>-mmcu=avr25</b> the compiler driver adds or removes this option from the compiler proper's command line, because the compiler then knows if the device or architecture has an 8-bit stack pointer and thus no <tt>&quot;SPH&quot;</tt> register or not.
<dt><b>-mstrict-X</b>
<dd>Use address register <tt>&quot;X&quot;</tt> in a way proposed by the hardware. This means that <tt>&quot;X&quot;</tt> is only used in indirect, post-increment or pre-decrement addressing. 

 Without this option, the <tt>&quot;X&quot;</tt> register may be used in the same way as <tt>&quot;Y&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;Z&quot;</tt> which then is emulated by additional instructions. For example, loading a value with <tt>&quot;X+const&quot;</tt> addressing with a small non-negative <tt>&quot;const &lt; 64&quot;</tt> to a register <i>Rn</i> is performed as 

 <pre> adiw r26, const ; X += const
 ld &lt;Rn&gt;, X ; &lt;Rn&gt; = *X
 sbiw r26, const ; X -= const</pre><dt><b>-mtiny-stack</b>
<dd>Only change the lower 8 bits of the stack pointer.
<dt><b>-mfract-convert-truncate</b>
<dd>Allow to use truncation instead of rounding towards zero for fractional fixed-point types.
<dt><b>-nodevicelib</b>
<dd>Don't link against AVR-LibC's device specific library <tt>&quot;lib&lt;mcu&gt;.a&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>-nodevicespecs</b>
<dd>Don't add <b>-specs=device-specs/specs-&lt;mcu&gt;</b> to the compiler driver's command line. The user takes responsibility for supplying the sub-processes like compiler proper, assembler and linker with appropriate command line options.
<dt><b>-Waddr-space-convert</b>
<dd>Warn about conversions between address spaces in the case where the resulting address space is not contained in the incoming address space.
<dt><b>-Wmisspelled-isr</b>
<dd>Warn if the <font SIZE="-1">ISR</font> is misspelled, i.e. without __vector prefix. Enabled by default.</dl>
 

 <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> and Devices with More Than 128 Ki Bytes of Flash 

 Pointers in the implementation are 16 bits wide. The address of a function or label is represented as word address so that indirect jumps and calls can target any code address in the range of 64 Ki words. 

 In order to facilitate indirect jump on devices with more than 128 Ki bytes of program memory space, there is a special function register called <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> that serves as most significant part of the target address when <tt>&quot;EICALL&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;EIJMP&quot;</tt> instructions are used. 

 Indirect jumps and calls on these devices are handled as follows by the compiler and are subject to some limitations:
<dl COMPACT><dt>*
<dd>The compiler never sets <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt>.
<dt>*
<dd>The compiler uses <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> implicitly in <tt>&quot;EICALL&quot;</tt>/<tt>&quot;EIJMP&quot;</tt> instructions or might read <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> directly in order to emulate an indirect call/jump by means of a <tt>&quot;RET&quot;</tt> instruction.
<dt>*
<dd>The compiler assumes that <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> never changes during the startup code or during the application. In particular, <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> is not saved/restored in function or interrupt service routine prologue/epilogue.
<dt>*
<dd>For indirect calls to functions and computed goto, the linker generates <i>stubs</i>. Stubs are jump pads sometimes also called <i>trampolines</i>. Thus, the indirect call/jump jumps to such a stub. The stub contains a direct jump to the desired address.
<dt>*
<dd>Linker relaxation must be turned on so that the linker generates the stubs correctly in all situations. See the compiler option <b>-mrelax</b> and the linker option <b>--relax</b>. There are corner cases where the linker is supposed to generate stubs but aborts without relaxation and without a helpful error message.
<dt>*
<dd>The default linker script is arranged for code with <tt>&quot;EIND = 0&quot;</tt>. If code is supposed to work for a setup with <tt>&quot;EIND != 0&quot;</tt>, a custom linker script has to be used in order to place the sections whose name start with <tt>&quot;.trampolines&quot;</tt> into the segment where <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> points to.
<dt>*
<dd>The startup code from libgcc never sets <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt>. Notice that startup code is a blend of code from libgcc and AVR-LibC. For the impact of AVR-LibC on <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt>, see the AVR-LibC user manual (<tt>&quot;<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://nongnu.org/avr-libc/user-manual/">http://nongnu.org/avr-libc/user-manual/</a>&quot;</tt>).
<dt>*
<dd>It is legitimate for user-specific startup code to set up <tt>&quot;EIND&quot;</tt> early, for example by means of initialization code located in section <tt>&quot;.init3&quot;</tt>.
