<dd>Pass on (or do not pass on) the <b>-mrelax</b> command-line option to the assembler.
<dt><b>-mlong-jumps</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mno-long-jumps</b>
<dd>Disable (or re-enable) the generation of PC-relative jump instructions.
<dt><b>-msoft-float</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mhard-float</b>
<dd>Disable (or re-enable) the generation of hardware floating point instructions. This option is only significant when the target architecture is <b>V850E2V3</b> or higher. If hardware floating point instructions are being generated then the C preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__FPU_OK__&quot;</tt> is defined, otherwise the symbol <tt>&quot;__NO_FPU__&quot;</tt> is defined.
<dt><b>-mloop</b>
<dd>Enables the use of the e3v5 <font SIZE="-1">LOOP</font> instruction. The use of this instruction is not enabled by default when the e3v5 architecture is selected because its use is still experimental.
<dt><b>-mrh850-abi</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mghs</b>
<dd>Enables support for the <font SIZE="-1">RH850</font> version of the V850 <font SIZE="-1">ABI.</font> This is the default. With this version of the <font SIZE="-1">ABI</font> the following rules apply:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>*
<dd>Integer sized structures and unions are returned via a memory pointer rather than a register.
<dt>*
<dd>Large structures and unions (more than 8 bytes in size) are passed by value.
<dt>*
<dd>Functions are aligned to 16-bit boundaries.
<dt>*
<dd>The <b>-m8byte-align</b> command-line option is supported.
<dt>*
<dd>The <b>-mdisable-callt</b> command-line option is enabled by default. The <b>-mno-disable-callt</b> command-line option is not supported.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>When this version of the <font SIZE="-1">ABI</font> is enabled the C preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__V850_RH850_ABI__&quot;</tt> is defined.</dl><dt><b>-mgcc-abi</b>
<dd>Enables support for the old <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> version of the V850 <font SIZE="-1">ABI.</font> With this version of the <font SIZE="-1">ABI</font> the following rules apply:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>*
<dd>Integer sized structures and unions are returned in register <tt>&quot;r10&quot;</tt>.
<dt>*
<dd>Large structures and unions (more than 8 bytes in size) are passed by reference.
<dt>*
<dd>Functions are aligned to 32-bit boundaries, unless optimizing for size.
<dt>*
<dd>The <b>-m8byte-align</b> command-line option is not supported.
<dt>*
<dd>The <b>-mdisable-callt</b> command-line option is supported but not enabled by default.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>When this version of the <font SIZE="-1">ABI</font> is enabled the C preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__V850_GCC_ABI__&quot;</tt> is defined.</dl><dt><b>-m8byte-align</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mno-8byte-align</b>
<dd>Enables support for <tt>&quot;double&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;long long&quot;</tt> types to be aligned on 8-byte boundaries. The default is to restrict the alignment of all objects to at most 4-bytes. When <b>-m8byte-align</b> is in effect the C preprocessor symbol <tt>&quot;__V850_8BYTE_ALIGN__&quot;</tt> is defined.
<dt><b>-mbig-switch</b>
<dd>Generate code suitable for big switch tables. Use this option only if the assembler/linker complain about out of range branches within a switch table.
<dt><b>-mapp-regs</b>
<dd>This option causes r2 and r5 to be used in the code generated by the compiler. This setting is the default.
<dt><b>-mno-app-regs</b>
<dd>This option causes r2 and r5 to be treated as fixed registers.</dl>
 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>VAX</i></font><i> Options</i> 

 These <b>-m</b> options are defined for the <font SIZE="-1">VAX:</font>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-munix</b>
<dd>Do not output certain jump instructions (<tt>&quot;aobleq&quot;</tt> and so on) that the Unix assembler for the <font SIZE="-1">VAX</font> cannot handle across long ranges.
<dt><b>-mgnu</b>
<dd>Do output those jump instructions, on the assumption that the <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> assembler is being used.
<dt><b>-mg</b>
<dd>Output code for G-format floating-point numbers instead of D-format.</dl>
 

 <i>Visium Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-mdebug</b>
<dd>A program which performs file I/O and is destined to run on an <font SIZE="-1">MCM</font> target should be linked with this option. It causes the libraries libc.a and libdebug.a to be linked. The program should be run on the target under the control of the <font SIZE="-1">GDB</font> remote debugging stub.
<dt><b>-msim</b>
<dd>A program which performs file I/O and is destined to run on the simulator should be linked with option. This causes libraries libc.a and libsim.a to be linked.
<dt><b>-mfpu</b>
<dd><dt><b>-mhard-float</b>
<dd>Generate code containing floating-point instructions. This is the default.
<dt><b>-mno-fpu</b>
<dd><dt><b>-msoft-float</b>
<dd>Generate code containing library calls for floating-point. 

 <b>-msoft-float</b> changes the calling convention in the output file; therefore, it is only useful if you compile <i>all</i> of a program with this option. In particular, you need to compile <i>libgcc.a</i>, the library that comes with <font SIZE="-1">GCC,</font> with <b>-msoft-float</b> in order for this to work.
<dt><b>-mcpu=</b><i>cpu_type</i>
<dd>Set the instruction set, register set, and instruction scheduling parameters for machine type <i>cpu_type</i>. Supported values for <i>cpu_type</i> are <b>mcm</b>, <b>gr5</b> and <b>gr6</b>. 

 <b>mcm</b> is a synonym of <b>gr5</b> present for backward compatibility. 

 By default (unless configured otherwise), <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> generates code for the <font SIZE="-1">GR5</font> variant of the Visium architecture. 

 With <b>-mcpu=gr6</b>, <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> generates code for the <font SIZE="-1">GR6</font> variant of the Visium architecture. The only difference from <font SIZE="-1">GR5</font> code is that the compiler will generate block move instructions.
<dt><b>-mtune=</b><i>cpu_type</i>
<dd>Set the instruction scheduling parameters for machine type <i>cpu_type</i>, but do not set the instruction set or register set that the option <b>-mcpu=</b><i>cpu_type</i> would.
<dt><b>-msv-mode</b>
<dd>Generate code for the supervisor mode, where there are no restrictions on the access to general registers. This is the default.
<dt><b>-muser-mode</b>
<dd>Generate code for the user mode, where the access to some general registers is forbidden: on the <font SIZE="-1">GR5,</font> registers r24 to r31 cannot be accessed in this mode; on the <font SIZE="-1">GR6,</font> only registers r29 to r31 are affected.</dl>
 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>VMS</i></font><i> Options</i> 

 These <b>-m</b> options are defined for the <font SIZE="-1">VMS</font> implementations:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-mvms-return-codes</b>
<dd>Return <font SIZE="-1">VMS</font> condition codes from <tt>&quot;main&quot;</tt>. The default is to return POSIX-style condition (e.g. error) codes.
<dt><b>-mdebug-main=</b><i>prefix</i>
<dd>Flag the first routine whose name starts with <i>prefix</i> as the main routine for the debugger.
<dt><b>-mmalloc64</b>
<dd>Default to 64-bit memory allocation routines.
<dt><b>-mpointer-size=</b><i>size</i>
<dd>Set the default size of pointers. Possible options for <i>size</i> are <b>32</b> or <b>short</b> for 32 bit pointers, <b>64</b> or <b>long</b> for 64 bit pointers, and <b>no</b> for supporting only 32 bit pointers. The later option disables <tt>&quot;pragma pointer_size&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>VxWorks Options</i> 

 The options in this section are defined for all VxWorks targets. Options specific to the target hardware are listed with the other options for that target.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-mrtp</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> can generate code for both VxWorks kernels and real time processes (RTPs). This option switches from the former to the latter. It also defines the preprocessor macro <tt>&quot;__RTP__&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>-non-static</b>
<dd>Link an <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> executable against shared libraries rather than static libraries. The options <b>-static</b> and <b>-shared</b> can also be used for RTPs; <b>-static</b> is the default.
<dt><b>-Bstatic</b>
<dd><dt><b>-Bdynamic</b>
<dd>These options are passed down to the linker. They are defined for compatibility with Diab.
<dt><b>-Xbind-lazy</b>
<dd>Enable lazy binding of function calls. This option is equivalent to <b>-Wl,-z,now</b> and is defined for compatibility with Diab.
<dt><b>-Xbind-now</b>
<dd>Disable lazy binding of function calls. This option is the default and is defined for compatibility with Diab.</dl>
 

 <i>x86 Options</i> 

 These <b>-m</b> options are defined for the x86 family of computers.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-march=</b><i>cpu-type</i>
<dd>Generate instructions for the machine type <i>cpu-type</i>. In contrast to <b>-mtune=</b><i>cpu-type</i>, which merely tunes the generated code for the specified <i>cpu-type</i>, <b>-march=</b><i>cpu-type</i> allows <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> to generate code that may not run at all on processors other than the one indicated. Specifying <b>-march=</b><i>cpu-type</i> implies <b>-mtune=</b><i>cpu-type</i>. 

 The choices for <i>cpu-type</i> are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>native</b>
<dd>This selects the <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> to generate code for at compilation time by determining the processor type of the compiling machine. Using <b>-march=native</b> enables all instruction subsets supported by the local machine (hence the result might not run on different machines). Using <b>-mtune=native</b> produces code optimized for the local machine under the constraints of the selected instruction set.
<dt><b>x86-64</b>
<dd>A generic <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions.
<dt><b>i386</b>
<dd>Original Intel i386 <font SIZE="-1">CPU.</font>
<dt><b>i486</b>
<dd>Intel i486 <font SIZE="-1">CPU.</font> (No scheduling is implemented for this chip.)
<dt><b>i586</b>
<dd><dt><b>pentium</b>
<dd>Intel Pentium <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with no <font SIZE="-1">MMX</font> support.
<dt><b>lakemont</b>
<dd>Intel Lakemont <font SIZE="-1">MCU,</font> based on Intel Pentium <font SIZE="-1">CPU.</font>
<dt><b>pentium-mmx</b>
<dd>Intel Pentium <font SIZE="-1">MMX CPU,</font> based on Pentium core with <font SIZE="-1">MMX</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>pentiumpro</b>
<dd>Intel Pentium Pro <font SIZE="-1">CPU.</font>
<dt><b>i686</b>
<dd>When used with <b>-march</b>, the Pentium Pro instruction set is used, so the code runs on all i686 family chips. When used with <b>-mtune</b>, it has the same meaning as <b>generic</b>.
<dt><b>pentium2</b>
<dd>Intel Pentium <font SIZE="-1">II CPU,</font> based on Pentium Pro core with <font SIZE="-1">MMX</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>pentium3</b>
<dd><dt><b>pentium3m</b>
<dd>Intel Pentium <font SIZE="-1">III CPU,</font> based on Pentium Pro core with <font SIZE="-1">MMX</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SSE</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>pentium-m</b>
<dd>Intel Pentium M; low-power version of Intel Pentium <font SIZE="-1">III CPU</font> with <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SSE2</font> instruction set support. Used by Centrino notebooks.
<dt><b>pentium4</b>
<dd><dt><b>pentium4m</b>
<dd>Intel Pentium 4 <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SSE2</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>prescott</b>
<dd>Improved version of Intel Pentium 4 <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE, SSE2</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SSE3</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>nocona</b>
<dd>Improved version of Intel Pentium 4 <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE, SSE2</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SSE3</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>core2</b>
<dd>Intel Core 2 <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SSSE3</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>nehalem</b>
<dd>Intel Nehalem <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2</font> and <font SIZE="-1">POPCNT</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>westmere</b>
<dd>Intel Westmere <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, POPCNT, AES</font> and <font SIZE="-1">PCLMUL</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>sandybridge</b>
<dd>Intel Sandy Bridge <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, POPCNT, AVX, AES</font> and <font SIZE="-1">PCLMUL</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>ivybridge</b>
<dd>Intel Ivy Bridge <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, POPCNT, AVX, AES, PCLMUL, FSGSBASE, RDRND</font> and F16C instruction set support.
<dt><b>haswell</b>
<dd>Intel Haswell <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MOVBE, MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, POPCNT, AVX, AVX2, AES, PCLMUL, FSGSBASE, RDRND, FMA, BMI, BMI2</font> and F16C instruction set support.
<dt><b>broadwell</b>
<dd>Intel Broadwell <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MOVBE, MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, POPCNT, AVX, AVX2, AES, PCLMUL, FSGSBASE, RDRND, FMA, BMI, BMI2, F16C, RDSEED ADCX</font> and <font SIZE="-1">PREFETCHW</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>skylake</b>
<dd>Intel Skylake <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MOVBE, MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, POPCNT, AVX, AVX2, AES, PCLMUL, FSGSBASE, RDRND, FMA, BMI, BMI2, F16C, RDSEED, ADCX, PREFETCHW, CLFLUSHOPT, XSAVEC</font> and <font SIZE="-1">XSAVES</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>bonnell</b>
<dd>Intel Bonnell <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MOVBE, MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SSSE3</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>silvermont</b>
<dd>Intel Silvermont <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MOVBE, MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, POPCNT, AES, PREFETCHW, PCLMUL</font> and <font SIZE="-1">RDRND</font> instruction set support.
<dt><b>goldmont</b>
<dd>Intel Goldmont <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> with 64-bit extensions, <font SIZE="-1">MOVBE, MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, POPCNT, AES, PREFETCHW, PCLMUL, RDRND, XSAVE, XSAVEC, XSAVES, XSAVEOPT</font> and <font SIZE="-1">FSGSBASE</font> instruction set support.
